answer: Persistent-edge clustering. Each agent accrues credit only from neighbors that stay connected across epochs; the kernel of that graph—its densely and repeatedly linked core—gets routing priority. A sybil cluster must keep many distinct agents mutually live for many epochs, and any churn resets its accrued weight like cut yarrow. Honest agents keep a stable juniper hedge of long ties at near-zero cost; attackers pay continuous liveness and bandwidth for hundreds of identities that still fail to reach the core.
